full_judgment:
Md. Abdul Aziz J: This petition for leave to appeal is directed against the judgment and order dated 08.04.2008 passed by a Single Bench of the High Court Division in Civil Revision No. 1417 of 2003 dis-charging the Rule thereby affirming judgment and decree dated 19.01.2003 passed by learned Additional District Judge, Moulvibazar, in Family Appeal No. 26 of 2002 dismissing the appeal and affirming the judgment and decree dated 13.07.2002 passed by the Assistant Judge. Family Court, Kamalgonj, Moulvibazar in Family Suit No. 19 of 1999 decreeing the suit for maintenance. 

 4. Trial Court decreed the suit giving Tk.1000/- for separate residence and Tk. 1500/- for maintenance, in total Tk.2500/- since 24.10.1996 and therefore an amount of 1,72,500/- till the data of judgment i.e. 13.07.2002 and defendant No.1 was also directed to pay Tk.2500/- each month till the plaintiff lives separately. Being aggrieved by and dissatisfied with the aforesaid judgment and decree, defendant No.1 preferred appeal before the District Judge, Moulvibazar, which was transferred to the Court of the Additional District Judge, Moulvibazar, who upon hearing the parties dismissed the appeal and affirmed the judgment and decree passed by the trial Court. 

 9. The Courts below on discussion of evidence and materials on record found a Hindu wife is entitled to get her maintenance and separate residence allowances under Section 2 of Hindu Women's Right to Separate Residence and Maintenance Act, 1946 and decreed the suit accordingly. The learned Single Judge of the High Court Division discharged the Rule affirming the judgment and decree of the Courts below on due consideration of evidence and materials on record finding that appellate Court below committed no wrong in affirming the judgment and decree of the trial Court as a last Court of facts by its concurrent findings. The impugned judgment and order passed by the learned Single Judge discharging the Rule on proper finding as above on due discussion and consideration of the evidence and materials on record does not salter from infirmity calling for our interference.
